newsitem.title: USA: Document says Spain received 85 tons of Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Document says Spain received 85 tons of Nazi gold.

text.p: Spain received 85 tons of gold from Nazi Germany during the Second World War, with the vast bulk of it shipped from Switzerland, according to a previously secret U.S. government document released on Wednesday by the World Jewish Congress.

The WJC, which has been combing the U.S. National Archives to trace Nazi financial dealings with neutral nations, said the document marked the first time a figure had surfaced on how much gold was shipped to Spain during the war.

A 1946 letter from the U.S. embassy in Madrid to the Secretary of State said 14 shipments were made, including deliveries by train and truck. The letter also spoke of a secret transfer of gold by Reichsbank President Walter Funk to Spanish accounts in Switzerland in which the gold was paid for in Spanish-held Swiss francs.

The document said that 74 tons of gold the Spanish received came via Switzerland and 11 tons from other nations. The Allies had warned Spain that it could not directly receive gold shipments from Germany.
Another document, a 1944 letter from U.S. Secretary of State Edward Stettinius to the Madrid embassy, said that Spanish fascists deposited "large sums in Argentine banks on behalf of the Nazis."
